title: Narrative Involvement
augmentation_provenance_exception: mediated-exegetical (Sartre/Iser → Phantasia Cluster) — applies ONLY to the Phantasia Cluster bridge anchored in the Synthesis subsection at book pp. 128-130
dimension_operational_definition: Narrative involvement is the player's engagement with story elements written into the game (scripted narrative) and with story elements that emerge from the player's moment-to-moment interaction with the game environment (alterbiography); macro phase = off-line anticipation and retrospection across sessions, micro phase = ongoing synthesis of rules, representation, and imagination into an unfolding causally-linked sequence.

boundary_criteria.criterion: Scripted vs. emergent provenance of story material
boundary_criteria.rule: If the segment was authored into the game by designers (cut scene, written quest text, in-world objects, dialog, verbal-text streams), classify as SCRIPTED NARRATIVE; if it is generated by the player's interpretation of and action within the environment, classify as ALTERBIOGRAPHY (book pp. 115, 119-120, 124-125).

Narrative involvement does NOT require Juul's story/discourse split: in games these times typically collapse, so the operative distinction is scripted/alterbiographic rather than story/discourse (pp. 114, 115).

boundary_criteria.criterion: Narrative experience vs. general gameplay thought
boundary_criteria.rule: Thoughts about the game system (e.g., poker bluff calculation) do NOT count as narrative experience; narrative experience requires a fictional environment with characters or world-elements supporting story-generation (pp. 117-119).

If story is imposed and suspends player action (cut scenes, quick-time events) classify push; if story is embedded in the world and elicits player effort to retrieve it (audio diaries, in-world books), classify pull (pp. 122-123).

Determine whether the player's alterbiography is FOCALIZED on self (first-person disposition), on a controlled entity (third-person disposition), or on a collective/managerial group; focalization is fixed by player disposition rather than by camera alone (pp. 124-126; Figure 7.1).
Quest goals belong to LUDIC when they function as reward-progression; the same quest text belongs to NARRATIVE when the player invests in its story content (p. 121).

concepts.label: Scripted narrative
concepts.definition: Story content and structures explicitly written into a game by designers; delivered via cut scenes, quick-time events, in-world objects, dialog, and verbal-text streams.

concepts.label: Alterbiography
concepts.definition: The ongoing narrative generated during the player's interaction with a game environment — a cyclical process afforded by representational, mechanical, and medium-specific qualities of the game and actuated in the player's mind.
concepts.introduction_anchor: italicized definitional prose at book p.115 (line 4013); dedicated subsection at book p.124

concepts.label: Alterbiography of self
concepts.definition: First-person disposition: player interprets in-game events as happening to herself rather than to an external character.

concepts.label: Alterbiography of entity
concepts.definition: Third-person disposition: alterbiography centers on a single controlled entity treated as distinct from the player.

concepts.label: Alterbiography of miniatures (managerial/environment focalization)
concepts.definition: Player controls multiple entities (RTS) or a non-individually-simulated collective (SimCity, Medieval II Total War campaign) — alterbiography focalized on the collective or managerial position.

concepts.label: Focalization (Genette)
concepts.definition: Restriction of field — perspective-filtering of fictional-world information. Calleja extends Genette's literary concept to game environments where camera + control-scheme + player-disposition jointly constitute focalization.

concepts.label: Push narrative
concepts.definition: Designer-imposed delivery in which the player is a captive audience (cut scenes, quick-time events); action suspended during delivery.

concepts.label: Pull narrative
concepts.definition: Designer-embedded narrative elements that rely on player effort to retrieve (audio diaries, in-world books); player elicits the story rather than receives it.

concepts.label: Scripted-narrative structures of progression
concepts.definition: Four-type typology of how scripted narrative is organized across a game's main path: linear; branching backbone with side quests; open with main story plus side stories; no main story with serially organized side quests.

concepts.label: Synthesis of rules + representation + imagination
concepts.definition: Player's interpretive combination of game-rule outputs, representational layer (visual/auditory/textual), and mental imagery into a coherent ongoing narrative segment; the first building block of alterbiography.

concepts.label: Narrative as cognitive / mental construct (Ryan)
concepts.definition: Ryan 2006's reframing of narrative as a cognitive construct applicable to varied media while sensitive to medium-specific qualities — Calleja's primary corrective to Juul + Eskelinen anti-narrative arguments.

concepts.label: Embedded vs emergent narrative (Salen + Zimmerman)
concepts.definition: Distinction between authored-into-the-game story material (embedded) and story material that emerges from systemic / dynamic / participatory gameplay structures (emergent); endorsed but qualified by Calleja.

concepts.label: Environmental storytelling / evocative spaces (Jenkins)
concepts.definition: Jenkins 2004's four spatial-narrative forms: evoking pre-existing associations; staging ground; embedded mise-en-scène; resources for emergent narrative — useful but limited to spatial dimension only.

concepts.label: Narrative affordances
concepts.definition: Story-generating properties of a game environment's interactional structure — Calleja uses 'affordance' generically, NOT cited to Gibson.

concepts.label: Ergodic anchoring of narrative (Aarseth)
concepts.definition: Narrative analysis in games must be anchored in mechanical, coded structures of ergodic texts rather than in surface signs alone — Calleja explicitly endorses.

concepts.label: Pearce's six narrative operators
concepts.definition: Experiential / performative / augmentary / descriptive / metastory / story-system — framework Calleja flags as over-general (applies to tic-tac-toe + basketball + Sims) and analytically limited.

concepts.label: Story-time vs discourse-time collapse in games (Juul critique)
concepts.definition: Juul 2001's observation that story-time and discourse-time are synchronous in games — Calleja accepts the observation but rejects Juul's conclusion that this incompatibility implies non-narrative status.

concepts.label: Narrative props (Walton)
concepts.definition: Borrowed from Walton 1990 — game-environment elements that make alterbiography-generation more likely.

concepts.label: Iser's phenomenology of synthesis
concepts.definition: Reader-response synthesis: connections formed by the reader that are neither solely in the text nor solely in imagination; projections of dual nature (emerge from reader + guided by textual signals). Cited directly. Mediated-exegetical bridge anchor.

concepts.label: Sartre on author/reader interdependence + ambiguity-revealed synthesis
concepts.definition: Sartre 1967 What Is Literature? quoted on writer/reader two-active-people interdependence; Sartre 1995 The Imaginary invoked on synthesis becoming apparent when representational qualities are ambiguous. Mediated-exegetical bridge anchor.

concepts.label: Macro-phase narrative involvement
concepts.definition: Off-line between-sessions anticipation and retrospection of scripted narrative + accumulated alterbiography ('wondering what might happen next').

concepts.label: Micro-phase narrative involvement (alterbiography-occurrence-locus)
concepts.definition: Moment-to-moment alterbiography generation through interpretation of game events. Calleja DECLARES this micro-phase location at p.131 line 4648 without a labeled Micro-Phase subsection — structural deviation from Ch.4-6/8-9 template.

concepts.label: Dissolves narratology-vs-ludology binary
concepts.definition: Calleja's meta-position: refuses both Juul/Eskelinen anti-narrative and broad attribute-everything-to-narrative positions; via Ryan's cognitive reframing plus the scripted/alterbiography distinction the debate is dissolved rather than mediated.

concepts.label: Scripted-narrative delivery channels
concepts.definition: Five-element inventory: cut scenes, quick-time events, in-world objects, dialog, verbal-text streams.

concepts.label: Designer-commentary as theoretical source
concepts.definition: Calleja explicitly draws on practicing-designer commentary (Sam Houser on GTA IV; Ken Levine on Bioshock) rather than exclusively academic sources — methodologically notable for the chapter.

concepts.label: Story-driven vs system-driven games
concepts.definition: Differentiation by whether progression couples ludic goal/reward with scripted-narrative advancement.

positions.label: Calleja DISSOLVES the narratology-vs-ludology binary
positions.stance: Rejects framing the debate via Juul + Eskelinen anti-narrative position using Ryan's cognitive-narrative reframing; endorses Salen+Zimmerman + Aarseth on importance of ergodic mechanical structures; extends both via the new scripted/alterbiography distinction. Effectively dissolves the binary rather than mediating it. Meta-position of the chapter.

positions.label: Alterbiography is the proper concept for emergent game narrative
positions.stance: Salen+Zimmerman 'emergent narrative' and Pearce 'experiential narrative' are useful but over-general; Jenkins is spatially restricted; Calleja's alterbiography concept supplies the cyclical-process specification (afforded by representational + mechanical + medium-specific qualities; actuated in player's mind) that the other frameworks lack.

positions.label: Scripted narrative and alterbiography are co-constitutive, not mutually exclusive
positions.stance: Alterbiography integrates scripted-narrative elements that relate to its focalized entity. Bioshock Dr. Steinman is the paradigm: pre-encounter audio-diary + poster + portrait priming becomes part of the player's alterbiography when the scripted surgery encounter occurs.

positions.label: Game-narrative experience must be grounded in cyber-textual qualities
positions.stance: Salen+Zimmerman's poker bluff-narrative example is rejected: thoughts about a game system do NOT count as narrative experience absent a fictional environment with characters or world-elements; the GTA IV Nico/Roman/Michelle extended walkthrough illustrates the proper grounding.

positions.label: Designer-commentary is admissible theoretical evidence
positions.stance: Sam Houser on GTA IV and Ken Levine on Bioshock are cited as primary sources for theoretical moves (designer-question reframing; push/pull distinction) — Calleja's methodological openness to practicing-designer discourse.

positions.label: Focalization is set by player disposition, not by camera or interface alone
positions.stance: First-person camera ≠ alterbiography-of-self automatically; football-manager player controlling a whole team may have managerial focalization; Medieval II:TW player may shift focalization mid-session. Disposition, not interface, governs.

tensions.label: Juul's story/discourse collapse argument vs Calleja's two-dimensional narrative distinction
tensions.calleja_resolution: Juul slides between two senses of narrative; the proper distinction is scripted-narrative vs alterbiography, not story-time vs discourse-time. The collapse Juul identifies pertains only to alterbiography, not to scripted narrative (where flashbacks/flashforwards remain operative — Max Payne, Call of Duty IV).

tensions.label: Eskelinen's self-undermining anti-narrative position
tensions.calleja_resolution: Eskelinen claims print narratology cannot apply to games while building his anti-narrative argument on claims from Genette + Prince (the most ardent literary narratologists). Calleja exposes the inconsistency rather than refuting Eskelinen on his own terms.

tensions.label: Experiential narrative scope: useful concept vs analytical redundancy
tensions.calleja_resolution: Pearce + Salen+Zimmerman stretch experiential narrative until it covers tic-tac-toe and poker; Calleja narrows by requiring grounding in fictional environment with characters or world-elements supporting story-generation (the cybertextual-qualities constraint).

tensions.label: Representational layer vs simulation rules in alterbiography-shaping
tensions.calleja_resolution: Alterbiography can be shaped by representational elements (e.g., Oblivion Redguard race interaction) that have NO corresponding simulation rule — player's interpretive disposition supplies the alterbiographic content the system does not.

tensions.label: Macro/micro template canon vs Ch.7 distributed micro-phase declaration
tensions.calleja_resolution: Ch.7 lacks an explicitly labeled Micro Phase: subsection (deviation from Ch.4-6/8-9 template); instead Calleja inserts a single declarative sentence at p.131 that 'alterbiography occurs in the micro phase of narrative involvement.' The structural anomaly is captured here as a Phase-3 ontology-synthesis concern.

burke_pentad_mapping.rationale: Alterbiography is the unfolding ACT-stream (what is done, in Burkean pentad terms); scripted narrative supplies PURPOSE (designer-imposed teleology — main quest, narrative goal). The Push and Pull Narrative subsection (pp.122-124) effectively dramatizes the Act/Purpose ratio: pushed narrative is Purpose-saturated and Act-constraining; pulled narrative releases Purpose to Player-Act. The Bioshock Steinman intersection (pp.132-133) is a Burkean Act/Purpose-ratio paradigm: pre-encounter Purpose-priming (audio-diaries) becomes Player-Act content when assimilated to alterbiography.
burke_pentad_mapping.exegetical_status: Burke wholly absent from Calleja (cite_check 0 hits)

uexkull_mapping.rationale: Alterbiography's central operation — stringing together causally-related segments of synthesis of interaction with and interpretation of game-elements — structurally parallels Uexküll's sequence of Bedeutungsträger within an Umwelt. NPCs, quest items, audio diaries, environmental details function as successive meaning-bearers. Pull narrative (Levine on Bioshock) maps especially well: player-pulled-Bedeutungsträger are biosemiotically active; pushed cut scenes function as designer-imposed non-Bedeutungsträger interruptions. Subordinate construct: Wirkmal-loop closure when player completes a scripted-narrative checkpoint.
uexkull_mapping.exegetical_status: Uexküll wholly absent from Calleja (cite_check 0 hits); Gibson-as-mediated-bridge hypothesis falsified at Phase 0

aristotelian_grounding.rationale: STRONGEST single-concept bridge in the chapter. Alterbiography is functionally Aristotelian muthos in everything but vocabulary — synthesis of incidents (kineseis) into a unified action with beginning, middle, and end (now distributed across game sessions). Calleja's Synthesis subsection (pp.128-130) makes this explicit at the cognitive level. Tabletop-RPG worked example (pp.129-130) presents muthos in miniature: declarative-action by player → causally-related segments of synthesis → mental image-sequence. Secondary anchor: Heidegger BCAP on time-phenomenology and kairotic event-structuring (parallels macro-phase off-line anticipation of scripted-narrative continuation and micro-phase moment-by-moment alterbiography generation).
aristotelian_grounding.exegetical_status: Aristotle wholly absent from Calleja; Heidegger present only at p.21 (Question Concerning Technology), does not appear in Ch.7

anchor_text_loci.calleja_move: Iser 1991 quoted directly on reader-synthesis (text neither expectation nor memory — reader must put together what wandering viewpoint has divided up; syntheses of dual nature, projections from reader plus textual signals).

Sartre 1967 What Is Literature? quoted directly on author/reader interdependence — 'the combined efforts of author and reader bring into being the concrete and imaginary object which is the work of the mind. Art exists only for and through other people.'
Sartre 1995 The Imaginary invoked on synthesizing efforts becoming apparent when representational qualities are ambiguous.

sartre_iser_phantasia_mediated_exegetica.rationale: Calleja directly cites Sartre's The Imaginary (1995) and What Is Literature?
